rows.verified: HSE Management Standards provide a step-by-step risk-assessment approach for work-related stress.
The approach can assess the current situation using existing data, surveys and other evidence.
The approach promotes discussion and partnership with employees and their representatives when selecting improvements.
The six Management Standards areas are demands, control, support, relationships, role and change.
Employers have a legal duty to protect workers from stress by carrying out a risk assessment and acting on it.
The Management Standards help organisations identify underlying causes rather than focusing only on individual symptoms.
The formal process includes identifying risk factors, identifying who may be harmed, evaluating risks, recording findings and monitoring and review.
HSE's workbook provides practical guidance and checklists that can be retained as evidence of the approach taken.
Work-stress risk depends on work design, workload, autonomy, support, relationships, role clarity, change and individual circumstances.
HSE stress evidence is organisation-, team-, role-, worker-, intervention- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level health probability.
A decision to use pesticides should follow a thorough risk assessment and form part of an integrated pest-management approach.
The placing on the market, storage, use and disposal of pesticides are controlled activities.
Professional users should buy only products authorised for storage and use in the UK and check the approval number on the label.
Pesticides should be stored in their original containers with the approved product labels and never decanted into drinks containers.
Pesticide stores should prevent unwanted releases, use non-combustible construction and be secured against unauthorised access.
Pesticides should not be carried in a tractor or vehicle cab; a separated, secure and leak-proof load arrangement should be used.
Users must understand and follow the product label, safety data sheet and required personal protective equipment.
Applications should be confined to the target area, carried out in suitable weather to minimise drift, and recorded.
Pesticide risk depends on product, formulation, dose, application equipment, weather, target, exposure route, PPE, storage and disposal.
HSE pesticide evidence is product-, operation-, worker-, environment-, control- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level poisoning probability.
